6.1.2.title: Journey Planning Procedure
6.1.2.text:
Journey plans are required where travel presents an elevated risk due to distance, duration,
road conditions, fatigue, remoteness, or environmental factors. The following conditions are
indicators of elevated risk and must be considered as part of journey risk assessment:

• Greater than 200kms on sealed roads
• 50km on unsealed roads), or
• 2 hours in length.

These indicators do not replace risk assessment and must not be used in isolation to
determine journey risk.

Journey Plans should include the following information:

• Departure and arrival times
• Estimated travel time
• Any expected delays or extension to trip duration due to personal diversions whilst in
transit
• Fatigue issues that may be associated with the reason for travel, and
• Potential weather conditions and wildlife exposure risks.

Drivers will not exceed a total of 10 hours a day driving while conducting Verra Mobility
business.

If either a notification of arrival or delays in transit are not notified to the Leader within 1
hour of the estimated arrival time the Leader should attempt to contact the driver.

4.1.2.title: Drivers
4.1.2.text:
Drivers are required to:

• Comply with this Procedure and all road rules
• Report vehicle defects, incidents, and hazards, and
• Cease driving where they are not fit to drive.

4.3.title: Fitness for Work Requirements
4.3.text:
4.3.1. Drivers
Drivers must:

• Be fit for work, including not driving while impaired by fatigue, alcohol (BAC of 0.00),
drugs, medication, or medical conditions,
• Refrain from road rage and aggressive driving.

4.2.1.title: Drivers
4.2.1.text:
Drivers are required to:

• Hold a current and valid license appropriate to the vehicle being driven, and
• Complete the Driving Training Module (IMS.03.06.TRN.01) annually.

6.1.1.title: Prestart Check Procedure
6.1.1.text:
A documented pre-start check shall be carried out daily prior to driving a vehicle using the
Vehicle Prestart Form (IMS.03.06.FRM.01).

Should any vehicle faults be identified during the pre-start check, the vehicle is to remain
stationary and identified as being out of service until a qualified mechanic diagnoses and  /
or repairs the problem and clears the vehicle for normal use.

Documented pre-start checks should include:

• A walk round visual check, looking for loose fittings, loose wheel nuts, broken lights and
panel damage
• Activate and check all lights work on the vehicle
• Record the pre-trip mileage
• Check the operation of the horn, brakes, steering and radio (if applicable)
• Check the fire extinguisher and first aid kit (where present)

• Note if the vehicle is dirty
• Note any defects which have occurred since the vehicle was last utilized, and
• Report to the Leader if the vehicle is unsafe to use and arrange to have the problem
rectified.

4.2.title: Competency Requirements
4.2.text:
4.2.1. Drivers
Drivers are required to:

• Hold a current and valid license appropriate to the vehicle being driven, and
• Complete the Driving Training Module (IMS.03.06.TRN.01) annually.

4.1.title: Specific Roles and Responsibilities Related to this Procedure
4.1.text:
4.1.1. Leaders
All Leaders are responsible for:

• Ensuring only authorised and licensed personnel undertake work-related driving
• Ensuring vehicles used for work are fit for purpose
• Managing work schedules to reduce fatigue-related risks
• Monitoring driving incidents and infringements, and
• Taking action where unsafe driving behaviour or elevated risk is identified.
4.1.2. Drivers
Drivers are required to:

• Comply with this Procedure and all road rules
• Report vehicle defects, incidents, and hazards, and
• Cease driving where they are not fit to drive.

6.2.title: Incident Hazards, Near Miss Reporting Procedure
6.2.text:
All Incidents, Near Misses and Hazards including those associated with environmental
occurrences with flora / flora shall be reported as per Incident, Near Miss and Hazard
Management Procedure (IMS.06.01.PRO.01).
